questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international student environment and the Italian culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really loved the city and the overall experience, but the course registration process was complicated and annoying.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. They had an online info meeting, but apart from that, the whole administrative process was quite complicated.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much assistance. I received a few emails, but with a long response time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find housing, as you need to be aware of the many scammers. However, through former exchange students, we got the contact details of a person who helped us find an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit expensive, and cleaning standards might be a bit different from what you're used to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I personally preferred living within the city walls, and it kept me close to everything.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was quite messy. There was an online check-in course upon arrival. The exact courses offered for the semester were released quite late, and it was a bit of a puzzle to get the schedule to work. Additionally, there were suddenly courses that you couldn't take, and 50% of our courses had to be from humanities. You also need to be prepared to change your learning agreement multiple times. But in the end, everything worked out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an email for exchange students and a coordinator available, but the response times were very long.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: After a lengthy process, I was eventually able to register for the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The rules for which courses you can take and which ones are available are constantly changing, so it can be quite a process. But be patient, as it will eventually work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There were different levels of courses, but overall, it was fine. Many of the courses were at a lower level compared to UCPH, which means it's possible for bachelor's students to take master's-level courses. However, you should be aware that sometimes they can be a bit strict about allowing bachelor students to take master's courses, although we were still allowed to enroll in them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different. There was more active participation, with presentations and class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Humanitarian Communication, China in Africa, Urban Studies and Climate Change, Introduction to Italian Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Humanitarian Communication had some interesting texts and content, but I didn’t always get much out of the lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinks, coffee, and eating out in general were cheaper than expected, but some supermarkets could be a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different opportunities, but a medical certificate was required for sports activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking in the Bologna hills, visiting Cinema Modernissimo, and taking various trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking trips to other cities. In the Dolomites, you can enjoy beautiful hiking routes, and you can also do day trips to cities like Florence, Parma, or Verona.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with exchange students, but there are chances to connect with local students during lectures and through group work.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find any cultural differences particularly challenging, but there could be a language barrier with the locals sometimes. It might be helpful to know some Italian.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture and, in general, the way Italians spend time socializing, whether it's going out for coffee, eating together, or having drinks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the process, everything will work out in the end! Explore different cities, and don’t forget to enjoy beautiful Bologna!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The administrative process can seem chaotic, but be patient because it will work out in the end.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The wonderful people I met and just all the amazing experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The course registration process and getting used to a new university with a very different structure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
